title: Licensing Regulations 1823
definition: A restrictive press policy introduced by Acting Governor-General John Adam, mandating that every printer and publisher obtain a government license to operate a press, effectively curbing the burgeoning Indian-language press.
importanceInUpsc: It marks the first major legislative attempt by the British to institutionalize censorship, serving as a precursor to the more draconian Vernacular Press Act of 1878.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Licensing Regulations 1823.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Role of Raja Ram Mohan Roy
British Administrative Policy under John Adam
